column2: Handscroll (青绿山水). The 2:1 glass is a window onto a Chinese blue-green landscape handscroll on aged silk: azurite and malachite peaks with gold contour lines and ink texture strokes (cun), drifting mist bands, a fisherman's skiff, a line of cranes, all panning in slow parallax at 60 fps. The numerals ARE mountains: craggy peaks whose silhouettes form the digits, designed as a set of ten landforms (the 0 a ring of cliffs round a lake, the 1 a single needle peak...), not a font with rock texture. Minute turn: the scroll unrolls onward (or mist swallows the old peak and the new one rises through it), the time never wrong. Hour: something bigger, e.g. a vermilion seal stamped onto the silk, or the sun/moon crossing. Day: silk warm by day, indigo ink-wash and a moon at night.

Jelly. Wobbly, glossy, translucent gelatin numerals: raspberry, lime, orange, made in fluted copper moulds, so the letterforms are moulded shapes (ridged, rounded, domed), with subsurface glow, a specular highlight and caustic light thrown through them onto the tablecloth. Soft-body physics: they jiggle on every second (a tap, a passing spoon, a heartbeat of the table), squash and recover with real damped springs. Minute turn: a spoon scoops the old digit away in wobbling bites, then a copper mould comes down, lifts, and the new jelly slumps out and jiggles to rest. Hour: something grand, e.g. a layered rainbow jelly tower unmoulded with a huge wobble. Don't copy mischief's row of ceramic numerals on a shelf: find a composition of your own (a plate, a cake stand, a tilted table top in perspective...).

Culture. A fluorescence microscope: the numerals are living cells, stained the way biologists do (GFP-green membranes, DAPI-blue nuclei, mCherry-red mitochondria) glowing on a deep, coloured dark field, with cytoplasm streaming, organelles drifting and small organisms (paramecia with beating cilia, diatoms) swimming past at 60 fps. The letterforms are cell bodies: blobby, membrane-bound, with nuclei placed to make the digits read. Minute turn: the changing digit-cell goes through mitosis (chromatin condenses into chromosomes, a spindle forms, a cleavage furrow pinches) and its daughter cell becomes the new digit; or the old cell flows by amoeboid pseudopods into the new shape. Hour: a bigger event (every digit divides in sync, a stain wash floods the field in a new colour, the stage pans to a new field). Maybe a microfluidic channel suits the 2:1 strip better than a round eyepiece.

Vector arcade. A colour vector-display arcade cabinet of 1979-83 (Asteroids, Tempest, Battlezone, Star Wars): the face is a beam-drawn screen, every line a glowing stroke with brighter vertices where the beam lingers, bloom, and phosphor persistence trails at 60 fps. The numerals are 3D wireframe objects drawn by the beam: designed vector digits (think Hershey strokes extruded into wireframe solids), slowly turning and drifting in space. A little ship patrols. Minute turn: the ship shoots the old digit, it shatters into tumbling line segments, and the debris flies back together into the new digit. Hour: a bigger show, e.g. a Tempest tube dive or a hyperspace jump, with the time still readable. Game details are welcome (score in vector type, lives as little ships), but the clock must be the clear hero. LCD black is a dark grey: make the dark deliberate (a deep blue-black tube with a faint curved glare, a bezel, a colour overlay like the Vectrex had).
